analysis.title: GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving
key_insights: GS desk expects equities to grind choppily moderately higher, with turbulence over the next two weeks. Systematic flows are skewed to the upside for the first time in weeks, and retail and corporates have defended their bid until the holidays.

Flows are split: retail has supported the market while institutions sold tech and cut leverage as the AI trade is tested. Net weekly and monthly flow totals look tame against large day-to-day reversals.
Prime book: Info Tech was the most net sold global and US sector for another week. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5 against a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June, the lowest on record since 2016.
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile one-year).
US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in 7 months, led by Large Cap Equity, Credit and Tech ETFs. Single stocks were heavily net sold (-1.7 SDs 1-year), driven mainly by short sales.

US-listed equity ETFs took in $59.3bn last week against $55.2bn the week before, beating 91% of the 46 weeks this year (weekly average $26.5bn). Fixed income ETF inflows fell to $2.6bn from $13.7bn, with net outflows Thursday and Friday after the hotter-than-expected CPI print.
Semis ETFs lost $7.3bn last week against an average weekly inflow of $6.2bn over the prior four weeks. $5.6bn left on Monday alone, followed by outflows on each of the last three days.

SOXL (3x bullish) took in $5.10bn in the Nov 5 week, its second-largest weekly inflow in a year, then lost $4.17bn the next week, its largest weekly outflow in a year. SOXS (3x bearish) had $4.38bn of outflows over two weeks and cut its share count by two-thirds. The desk reads levered ETF flows as a sign of low conviction.

Global equity funds had net inflows of $98bn in the week ending Nov 11 (vs $89bn the prior week), driven by US funds. Foreign flows have returned to the US, as in past election years, lifting the 4-week moving average by about $5bn.
Money market fund assets fell $18bn. GS rates strategists attribute softer AUM growth to firm risk asset returns and higher yields further out the curve.

Retail net bought $6.19bn of US equities, the largest weekly total of the 11 weeks since Sep 1, after +$0.12bn the week before. Retail share of notional traded was 9.01% (peak 10.0% on Nov 12). Buying concentrated in Nvidia (+$1.75bn), AMD (+$672mm), Micron (+$526mm) and Tesla (+$523mm).

Retail activity typically rises into Thanksgiving, dips during Thanksgiving week, rises again in mid-December and fades over the holidays. The desk says losing retail support could sharply change the US equity setup into year-end.

Corporate buybacks: desk volumes are 1.3x the 2025 YTD and 2024 YTD ADTV, skewed to Industrials, Energy and Financials. About 94% of the S&P 500 is in an open window (about 95% by week end), expected to stay open until December 13. 2026 YTD authorizations are $1.52T vs $1.27T in 2025 YTD. November is historically the second most active month for the desk, with over 10% of annual spend.

CTAs sold over $22bn of S&P and almost $2.5bn of Nasdaq last week, leaving US equity positioning short almost $10bn, the lowest since April. They are projected to buy almost $10bn of US equities over the next week in a flat tape ($8bn over 1m).

CTA projections, 1 week: flat tape buyers $22.97B ($9.86B US), up tape buyers $30.78B ($16.1B US), down tape sellers $6.07B ($5.23B US). 1 month: flat buyers $13.87B ($8.01B US), up buyers $89.1B ($54.04B US), down sellers $122.97B ($20.31B US).

Vol control and risk parity funds sold over $30bn combined last week. After CPI, stocks and bonds fell together, which typically makes risk parity cut exposure, though the desk expects this to be gradual. Vol control may re-risk in December/January if the market calms.

GS Panic Index is 6.3/10, in the 67th percentile on a 1y lookback. VIX volatility and SPX skew rose from the 12th and 38th percentiles on Nov 11 to the 59th and 67th. The vol forecast points to elevated volatility and choppy conditions near term.
Liquidity: top of book liquidity has stayed robust but is trending lower into the holiday season, with holiday closures weakening liquidity around them.

Seasonality: since 1990, in the 17 years when VIX started mid-November at 18 or higher, it was lower by year-end in 14, by 3.25 pts on average. SPX year-end gain in those years averaged +1.34% (up in 59% of years), with a median in-window drawdown of -3.0%. From Dec 15 to year-end the mean gain is +1.22%, with SPX up in 27 of 36 years.

sector_views.rationale: Institutional investors were the most net sold in US and global Info Tech on the prime book, with the US Info Tech long/short ratio at a record low of 1.5.
Semis ETFs lost $7.3bn last week against an average inflow of $6.2bn, while retail bought Nvidia, AMD and Micron.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hotter-than-expected print was followed by fixed income ETF outflows and stocks and bonds falling together, which pushes risk parity funds to cut exposure.

risk_factors: The next two weeks have historically been turbulent, and the tape has violent day-to-day reversals and rotations.
Retail support could fade if this week's test disappoints, which could change the US equity setup into year-end.
Systematic flow skew can reverse quickly if the tape turns down.
Continued institutional selling of tech amid broader AI spending concerns.
vol_and_positioning: GS Panic Index 6.3/10, 67th percentile on a 1y lookback.
VIX volatility moved from the 12th to the 59th percentile and SPX skew from the 38th to the 67th between Nov 11 and Nov 13 (rolling 2y lookback).
US Fundamental L/S net leverage 45.4% (4th percentile one-year), gross 209.1% (34th percentile).
CTA US equity positioning is short almost $10bn, the lowest since April.
Vol control and risk parity funds sold over $30bn combined over the past week.
With institutional positioning light, the desk argues a sustained move lower is unlikely without a move higher first.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail net bought $6.19bn of US equities, led by Nvidia, AMD and Micron. CTAs are projected buyers in a flat tape and corporate buyback windows are open.
tension_points.bear_case: Institutions sold tech and cut leverage, the US Info Tech long/short ratio is a record low 1.5, semis ETFs lost $7.3bn and the AI trade is being tested on spending concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail reducing buying this week, which the desk says could drastically change the US equity setup into year-end.

theme_stances.key_argument: Systematic flows are skewed to the upside for the first time in weeks while retail and corporates defend their bid, and light institutional positioning makes a sustained drop hard without a rise first.
theme_stances.evidence: equities will choppily grind moderately higher from here

theme_stances.key_argument: Institutional investors sold tech and removed leverage as conviction in the AI trade cracked on broader spending concerns.
theme_stances.evidence: Investor conviction in the market’s biggest trade has started to crack
